answer: Tying each key's bond to the machine that runs it lets an agent economy resist sybils. Every agent signs a hardware quote for its host, and a host's k-th key locks 12×k² POA: a lone agent locks 12 and the 30th key 10,800, so a farm called falcon running 1,000 keys on one rack locks about 4 billion to chase a reward oasis near 0.5 million per epoch. Renting many hosts resets k, so a similarity scan acts as a lantern: keys whose outputs match are merged and repriced as one host. A spoofed quote forfeits the whole bond. Limit: honest tenants of big clouds pay more.
